propositions: A drainer process dying between lock acquire and release leaves a 0-byte lock file permanently; subsequent drain attempts fail on FileExistsError with no staleness check and return skipped silently at INFO level, wedging enrichment indefinitely.

The drain lock lacks ownership metadata (v2 stamp with host/namespace/pid/start) that would allow detecting dead holders and reclaiming stale locks, unlike the mkdir write lock which already has this discipline.

Lock reclaim must distinguish live pid holders from dead ones and unknown/unstamped orphans using a shared core function (_stamp_is_stale) extracted from existing mkdir lock logic, with an unrecognised_via_ceiling parameter routing pre-existing orphans to the wall-clock ceiling.

On FileExistsError during acquire, check staleness via stamped_file_is_stale(); if stale log WARNING with holder+age, unlink, and retry exactly once; a second collision means another drainer won the race so return None.
Skip logs must move from INFO to WARNING and name the holder/age so wedges are visible without running doctor; a stamped acquired lock proves ownership by parsing as v2 stamp with local pid.
